record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can one develop a perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ and interacting-particle models analogous to KAM theory, so that one can study persistence of integrable structures and robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena under perturbation?

evidence.quote: Developing such a perturbation theory is an open conceptual and technical problem of the first order.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality class encompasses a wide family of stochastic growth and interacting-particle models (e.g. the asymmetric simple exclusion process, last-passage percolation with exponential weights, the polynuclear growth model, the narrow-wedge KPZ equation) whose one-point fluctuations on the characteristic scale t^{1/3} are conjectured to converge to Tracy–Widom-type distributions, with two-point statistics governed by the Airy processes. For a distinguished subfamily of "solvable" or "integrable" models, exact algebraic structures (determinantal/Pfaffian point processes, Bethe-ansatz eigenfunctions, Macdonald processes, Yang–Baxter integrability) make it possible to prove these limits rigorously. For generic "non-solvable" perturbations of such models (for example, exclusion processes with general jump rates, last-passage models with non-exponential weights, or ballistic deposition models), the exact algebraic structure is destroyed and the asymptotic scaling theorems are not known.

In a parallel classical setting, KAM (Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser) theory provides a perturbation theory for integrable Hamiltonian systems: although a small generic perturbation destroys exact integrability, a positive-measure set of invariant tori (and hence quasi-periodic motions) persists, yielding a robust description of the perturbed dynamics close to the integrable structure.

Problem. Develop a perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-class stochastic growth and interacting-particle models that plays a role analogous to KAM theory for Hamiltonian dynamics. Concretely, formulate and prove a framework in which:
(i) one specifies a class of "integrable" reference models in the KPZ class together with an admissible class of perturbations;
(ii) one identifies which integrable structures (e.g. determinantal correlations, exactly solvable transition operators, hidden symmetries) persist, in a suitably weakened or asymptotic sense, under small perturbations;
(iii) one establishes the robustness of the conjectured KPZ scaling exponents (1:2:3) and of the limiting fluctuation distributions (Tracy–Widom GUE/GOE, Baik–Rains, Airy_2, Airy_1, KPZ fixed point) under such perturbations, with quantitative control on the size of admissible perturbations.

Either provide such a perturbation theory together with at least one nontrivial theorem proving persistence of KPZ asymptotic scaling phenomena for a non-solvable perturbation of a solvable model, or prove an obstruction showing no such KAM-style theory can exist in the stated generality.
artifact.category_tag: KPZ universality and integrable perturbation theory
artifact.status_search_result: No KAM-style perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-class models is known. Surveys and lecture notes on KPZ universality (Corwin, Quastel, Sasamoto, Petrov) emphasize that proving KPZ asymptotics persists outside of solvable models—e.g., for last-passage percolation with non-exponential weights or for ballistic deposition—remains a central open problem, and no general perturbative framework analogous to KAM has been established.

status_evidence.title: Kardar-Parisi-Zhang Universality (Corwin)
status_evidence.snippet: Showing KPZ behavior persists when the distribution of weights is no longer exponential is a compelling and entirely open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Persistence of KPZ scaling under perturbations of solvable models is recognized as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to KPZ (Quastel)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of KPZ class: exact results restricted to integrable models; universality for generic models is largely conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: No general perturbation theory is available for non-solvable KPZ models.

status_evidence.title: All roads to the KPZ universality class (Petrov)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent lectures (2025) emphasize integrable probability as the main rigorous route, with universality for generic models remaining open.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025 no KAM-like perturbation framework for KPZ models is established.
